messages:
Marta: alert from runtime-monitor: sudden spike of CUDA illegal memory access on gpu-pool-3 — ~120 errors in last 5m, a few containers crashed. Logs show 'invalid device address' and pagewalk faults. tagging on-call.

incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-030: GPU addr-translation-fault — priority P1. Paging: possible kernel/userland race.

Pawan: taking this. quick ask: which models / routes? any customer-facing 5xxs?

Marta: affected routes: /v1/generate for models: redwood-7b-q4, open-13b-q8 on pool-3 nodes. Error surfaced after the 02:10 deploy to pool-3 (driver bump + cuBLAS 13.1 -> 13.2). Customers reporting 503s: acme-corp, nova-ml, beta-ux.

Kevin: oncall here too — seeing container OOMs and then CUDA illegal memory access. I grabbed dmesg from node gpu-3-17: 

```
[ 1024.512345] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=24213, gpu=0: E C 0 0 0 1 0 0
[ 1024.512350] kernel: BUG: misaligned address during pagewalk at 0x7ffd...
[ 1024.512355] cuda: illegal memory access (reason: misaligned addr) at kernel/fb/pagewalk.c:234
[ 1024.512360] container 24213 (runner) terminated with signal 11
```

Kevin: stack trace points to pagewalk() in our runtime's device-mmap path. The timing matches heavy KV-cache activity.

Dana: rolling back that driver in staging now. If this is driver/ABI-related we should fail back to previous driver and hold the deploy.

Pawan: immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon gpu-3-17 and drain; 2) revert driver on pool-3 to 535.x (previous); 3) enable model fallback to cpu or quantized variant for affected tenants; 4) notify customers. Who's on rollback?

Marta: I'm on rollback for pool-3 nodes. Starting with one node to validate.

deploy-bot: Revert request posted: rollback-driver pool=pool-3 target=535.86 user=Marta. ETA ~7m.

Pawan: also enable runtime safety: set ROUTING_POLICY for acme-corp/nova-ml to use dedicated-pool-1 and enable soft-fallback: max-retries=2, fallback-model=redwood-7b-q4a.

Kevin: grabbing container logs for a crashed pod: 

```
[2026-03-12T02:11:09Z] runtime: attempt 3: batch_size=8 seq_len=1024
E CudaError: illegal memory access during attention softmax
stack: runtime/attn.cu:412 -> runtime/execution.c:210 -> agent/serve.c:128
```

Kevin: likely a kernel/hardware/driver race — we need to escalate to infra-kernel if rollback doesn't stop it.

Marta: rollback succeeded on gpu-3-17, restarted pods: initial 5 requests looked green. rolling to 2 more nodes.

Pawan: good. keep throttling traffic until we verify. Dana, can you run a short load test against pool-3 with the old driver? want to reproduce.

Dana: running 10m synthetic load against heavy KV prompts now. will post results.

(7m later)

Dana: load test looks stable on reverted driver for 10m, no illegal-access errors on tested nodes.

Pawan: OK, mitigation effective. Next: postmortem plan and customer comms. Marta, please collect the node-level artifacts (dmesg, kernel oops, container logs). Kevin, can you save the model-level traces and the exact request that reproducibly triggered it?

Marta: saving artifacts to /srv/incidents/INC-2026-030/gpu-3-17/ (dmesg, nvcrash, container logs).

Kevin: saved reproducer and traced sequence. attaching short script to reproduce locally: 

```
# repro.sh
python run_batch.py --model redwood-7b-q4 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --pattern "kv-heavy"
```

Kevin: reproduced on staging when driver bumped to 13.2. Not reproducible on 13.1.

Pawan: escalation decision: hold driver 13.2 for pool-3, open ticket with driver vendor & infra-kernel team with full artifacts and repro. Postmortem owners: Marta (runtime), Kevin (repro & models), Pawan (incident lead).

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-030 status: mitigated -> partial mitigation confirmed. Next step: vendor escalation and PMR.

Marta: customer outreach draft: "We observed a transient runtime failure causing 503s for high-throughput requests on gpu-pool-3 due to an address-translation issue triggered after a recent driver update. We rolled back the driver and traffic is restored. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with a timeline and remediation." Any edits?

Kevin: add: "No data loss; requests that errored can be retried; we provided temporary routing/fallbacks for affected tenants."

Pawan: send comms after we confirm full pool rollout. Also schedule an urgent hotfix window for the driver once vendor confirms patch.

Dana: created vendor ticket DT-8891 with attached dmesg, nvcrash, reproducer.

Marta: closing this thread for live mitigation. We'll keep INC-2026-030 open for vendor follow-up and postmortem. Thanks everyone. :tada:
